set.question: Which sentence expresses probability?
options: Probablemente habrá más cambios. [There will probably be more changes.]
Habrá más cambios en la sociedad. [There will be more changes in society.]
Hubo más cambios en la sociedad. [There were more changes in society.]

set.question: Which sentence expresses a hypothetical situation?
options: Si cambiara la sociedad, tendríamos que adaptarnos. [If society changed, we would have to adapt.]
La sociedad cambiará durante los próximos años. [Society will change over the coming years.]
La sociedad ha cambiado mucho en los últimos años. [Society has changed a lot in recent years.]

set.question: Which sentence combines prediction and uncertainty?
options: Creo que habrá cambios, aunque no sabemos exactamente cuáles. [I think there will be changes, although we do not know exactly which ones.]
Habrá muchos cambios en el trabajo según todos los expertos. [There will be many changes in work according to all experts.]
Ahora no hay cambios en las costumbres de la gente. [Now there are no changes in people's habits.]

set.question: Which sentence best integrates the unit?
options: Probablemente habrá cambios, y es importante que nos preparemos para diferentes escenarios. [There will probably be changes, and it is important that we prepare for different scenarios.]
Habrá muchos cambios en la organización del trabajo según todos los expertos. [There will be many changes in work organisation according to all experts.]
El futuro de la sociedad depende de las decisiones que tomamos todos los días. [The future of society depends on the decisions we make every day.]

set.question: Which statement best combines prediction and preparation?
options: Aunque no sabemos exactamente qué ocurrirá, es importante que nos preparemos. [Although we do not know exactly what will happen, it is important that we prepare.]
Sabemos exactamente qué ocurrirá en los próximos años gracias a los expertos. [We know exactly what will happen in the coming years thanks to the experts.]
No resulta necesario preparar ningún plan especial porque las cosas no van a cambiar. [It does not turn out necessary to prepare any special plan because things are not going to change.]

old: "Use the simple future to make predictions about society and to describe what will happen later."
new: "You know the simple future from A2 Unit 19. Use it to make predictions about society and to describe what will happen later."

old: "For predictions with no fixed timeframe — what society *will* look like someday — the simple future fits better than *ir* *a* + infinitive, which suggests a nearer, already-planned future."
new: "For predictions with no fixed time, the simple future fits better than *ir a* + infinitive, which suggests a nearer, already planned future."

old: "Combine the future with expressions of probability such as *probablemente*, seguramente, *quizá* and es *posible* *que*."
new: "You know the future from A2 Unit 19, and *quizá* and *es posible que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 25. Combine them with *probablemente* to say how likely a prediction is."

old: "Quizá la gente trabajará menos horas en el futuro."
new: "Quizá la gente trabaje menos horas en el futuro."

old: "Es *posible* *que* forces the subjunctive (*sea*), but *probablemente* and *quizá* don't — they can sit comfortably in front of an ordinary future-tense verb."
new: "*Es posible que* and *quizá* take the subjunctive (*sea*, *trabaje*), but *probablemente* can sit in front of an ordinary future (*habrá*)."

old: "Use si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional to discuss possible changes and their consequences."
new: "You know *si* + imperfect subjunctive + conditional from B1 Unit 7. Use it to discuss possible changes and their consequences."

old: "Both clauses shift together: *cambiara* leaves the indicative because the whole scenario is imagined, which is why *tendríamos* also has to leave the simple future and move to the conditional."
new: "The whole scenario is imagined: *cambiara* is subjunctive, so the result is in the conditional (*tendríamos*), not in the simple future."

old: "Use es *necesario* *que*, es *importante* que and *hace* *falta* que with the subjunctive to discuss preparation for future changes."
new: "You know *es importante que* + subjunctive from A2 Unit 27. *Es necesario que* and *hace falta que* work the same way: use them to discuss preparation for future changes."

old: "English can say 'it's necessary that society prepares' with barely a verb change — Spanish can't skip the subjunctive here: es *necesario* *que* *preparemos*, never que preparamos."
new: "Spanish cannot skip the subjunctive here: *es necesario que preparemos*, never *que preparamos*."

old: "Combine predictions, probability, hypothetical language and necessity to discuss possible futures and defend a position."
new: "You know every structure here: the future (A2 Unit 19), *es importante que* (A2 Unit 27), *es posible que* (B1 Unit 25) and *si* + imperfect subjunctive (B1 Unit 7). Combine them to discuss possible futures and defend a position."

old: "Notice how *probablemente* and es *necesario* *que* can share a sentence: the first clause stays in the indicative future, the second switches to the subjunctive, and *así* *que* is what links the two."
new: "*Probablemente* and *es necesario que* can share a sentence: the first clause is in the future indicative, the second switches to the subjunctive, and *así que* links the two."
